learningObjectives: Identify accessibility issues across visual, auditory, motor, and cognitive experiences.
Apply inclusive interaction and content patterns.
Evaluate interfaces using accessibility-focused design criteria.

activities.title: Accessibility Needs Map
activities.instruction: Explore different accessibility needs and the design responses that support them.

content.concept: Inclusive design considers diverse sensory, motor, cognitive, and communication needs throughout the experience.
content.tip: Select each need to discover practical design responses.

items.label: Visual
items.description: Use sufficient contrast, scalable text, meaningful structure, and non-color indicators.

items.label: Auditory
items.description: Provide captions, transcripts, and visual alternatives for important audio information.

items.label: Motor
items.description: Support keyboard navigation, adequate target sizes, and alternatives to precise gestures.

items.label: Cognitive
items.description: Use clear language, predictable navigation, manageable choices, and helpful error recovery.

items.label: Communication
items.description: Present information through multiple understandable channels where appropriate.

activities.title: Accessible Pattern Matcher
activities.instruction: Match each accessibility barrier with an appropriate design solution.

content.concept: Accessible patterns can include keyboard support, clear labels, sufficient contrast, captions, focus indicators, and understandable feedback.
content.tip: Identify the barrier first, then select the pattern that directly addresses it.

pairs.prompt: A video contains important spoken instructions but has no captions.
A form field is identified only by placeholder text.
Keyboard users cannot see which control currently has focus.
An error is communicated only by changing text color to red.
Interactive controls require precise mouse movement.

activities.title: Keyboard Navigation Lab
activities.instruction: Arrange the correct keyboard focus sequence for the interface.

content.concept: Logical focus order allows keyboard users to navigate and operate interface controls predictably.
content.tip: Follow the visual and task order instead of jumping randomly between controls.

activities.title: Accessibility Audit
activities.instruction: Identify the accessibility issues in each interface scenario.

content.concept: An accessibility audit checks visual, interaction, content, navigation, and feedback patterns for barriers.
content.tip: Look beyond visual appearance and consider how different users operate the interface.

scenarios.question: A button has light gray text on a white background.
scenarios.explanation: Low contrast can make text difficult to perceive.

scenarios.question: A form error is indicated only with a red border.
scenarios.explanation: Important feedback should not depend on color alone.

scenarios.question: A modal opens but keyboard focus remains behind the modal.
scenarios.explanation: Keyboard focus should move appropriately into the active modal.
